correctness.rationale: In the exact package certificate.py, the prime-power theorem reduces nonzero candidates to exactly 256 sets; integer affine enumeration partitions them into three distinct orbits (64,128,64). Explicit frequency witnesses give strictly negative determinants of the threshold-shifted Hermitian Gram for the first two orbit representatives, and all 1820 supports of the last representative pass four exact positive Sylvester minors each. Integer-ring cyclotomic determinant arithmetic, algebraic reality assertions and certified radical enclosures make the signs rigorous. Separate complex Jacobi eigenvalue computations agree diagnostically. Every quantifier and Fourier normalization is specified.

residual_risks: An unindexed table, appendix, thesis, or unpublished exhaustive stability computation might already distinguish the order-sixteen full-spark orbits.
The exact certified threshold determines the optimizer class but not an algebraic expression for the optimal least squared singular value.

value.rationale: Worst-support squared lower singular value is a canonical noise-stability objective for four samples reconstructing an arbitrary four-frequency signal. Earlier qualitative full-spark results leave 256 feasible sets; the new natural complete finite classification selects exactly 64 nonconsecutive optimizer sets, rigorously ruling out all 1756 competitors. It is an informative robustness boundary for the canonical first few nontrivial dyadic Fourier sampling designs, not a mere parameter renaming or a selected unmotivated slice.
